19990-little-abe-or-the-bishop-of-berry-:
Little Abe tells the life of Abraham Lockwood, called the Bishop of Berry Brow. Berry Brow is a Yorkshire village of no pretensions to importance. Its only public building is a Mechanics' Institute of moderate size. One main street, substantially built, holds its life together. From these modest facts rises a local Methodist saint. F. Jewell wrote the life for the Methodist New Connexion. Small places made such bishops in that world.

Lockwood was a working preacher whose parish was one village. His monument is a life, not a building. Jewell's biography records sermons, conversions, and visitations in detail. It shows Wesleyan religion at its most local. Readers meet Victorian faith far below the famous pulpits. Little Abe's fame never left Yorkshire, which is the point.

govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HuieWilliamBrad: An excerpt preserves the prologue of He Slew the Dreamer, William Bradford Huie's book on the killing of Martin Luther King Jr. The identification of the excerpt is marked probable in the record rather than certain. narrative-of-services-in-the-liberation-:
Thomas Cochrane, Earl of Dundonald, tells of freeing South America by sea. This second volume, dated 1859, turns to Brazil's war. Don Pedro was proclaimed Emperor of Brazil in its first chapter. Brazil then sought foreign officers and seamen in haste.

The naval command was offered to Cochrane, and he accepted. At Rio he found poor ships and worse crews. Officials tried to cut the pay they had promised him. He refused a sham commission and forced fair terms. Then he blockaded Bahia and rigged fireships that scared the Portuguese fleet. Cochrane's own tale is bold, proud, and full of fight.
nasa-tm-19650015948-preliminary-operatio:
William R Kerslake at Lewis Research Center reported early test results in June 1965 for a new kind of cathode. The device is a wire brush coated with a thick oxide film. It was tried inside electron-bombardment ion thrustors, early electric engines for spacecraft. The summary says the first results pointed to longer thrustor life.

Cathode life limits how long an ion engine can run. A brush form gives a large working surface in a small space. Kerslake presents the operation as preliminary, not final proof. Even so, longer life was a key goal for engines meant to fire gently for months in space.
the-pony-rider-boys-in-the-grand-canyon-:
Frank Gee Patchin's The Pony Rider Boys in the Grand Canyon, or The Mystery of Bright Angel Gulch, lists twenty-four chapters before the story starts. Titles promise a night in the crater and an escape wholly cut off. They promise a battle with the roaring Colorado, dogs picking up a trail, and a new way to hunt lions. The home of the Havasupais appears, and Stacy as an Indian fighter.

Chapter I, Westward Ho!, opens at home rather than in the canyon. Tad Butler is chopping wood behind the woodshed. He finishes a tough, knotted stick before he looks up at the chorus of yells behind him. Three brown-faced young men, his companions of earlier rides, are regarding him solemnly. Patchin begins each series volume with the boys together and the road ahead. The chapter list makes clear that the canyon itself will supply the dangers this time.
the-private-diary-of-dr-john-dee-and-the: The Private Diary of Dr. John Dee and the Catalogue of His Library of Manuscripts were printed for the Camden Society from the originals in the Ashmolean Museum and Trinity College, Cambridge. James Orchard Halliwell edited the volume. A transcriber's note explains that Dee's Greek-script English is shown in Rotate-13 code, and diary footnotes take small letters while catalogue notes are numbered. The pages provided hold that note and the title page; the diary entries themselves are not among them.
